A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same fluorescent-ink adversarial attack, renamed from ITPATCH to FIPatch. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original fluorescence simulations, classifier attacks, physical experiments, sensitivity analyses, selective-trigger demonstrations, and defense evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains original digital and physical experimental results and adds UV-lamp-distance results in Appendix D and additional position-analysis heatmaps.

M1.justification: The documented misrecognition loss changes from -log(p_y) under minimization in v1 Equation 14 to log(p_y) in v2 Equation 11, correcting the optimization direction. Localization, fluorescence modeling, PSO, and robustness transformations otherwise remain the same. The PDFs do not establish whether this correction changed the implementation.

E1.justification: GTSRB, CTSRD, and the three attack tasks remain. v2 adds lamp-to-sign distance conditions through its 1–8 m experiment, but removes the time-specific and vehicle-specific evaluations from v1 Section 6.2.3 and Figure 18. The proposed drone deployment is not evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated defenses remain image smoothing, feature compression, input randomization, adversarial training, and defensive dropout (v1 Table 7; v2 Table 4). The removed comparison table in v1 summarizes prior work rather than reporting evaluated attack baselines.

E3.justification: The new Appendix D experiment fixes the vehicle at 10 m and 30 degrees, ambient illumination at 150 lux, and patch radius at 14 cm, while testing lamp distances of 1, 2, 4, 6, and 8 m. Retained experiments preserve their stated image sizes, detection threshold, PSO restarts, and iteration counts.

E4.justification: v2 adds robustness analysis of lamp-to-sign distance and extends position sensitivity from CNN and ResNet50 to VGG16 and GoogleNet in Figure 15. It removes the selective-trigger case studies in v1 Figure 18. Existing vehicle-distance/angle analyses are retained and redisplayed, not newly added.

E5.justification: There are no changes to repeated-evaluation or seed disclosures, significance testing, or uncertainty-estimation practices. The existing shape-analysis boxplots are retained, and the new table and heatmaps introduce no additional uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 Table 7 adds 8 m ASRs of 87%, 84%, 90%, and 81% for ResNet50, VGG13, CNN, and GoogleNet, respectively, under new conditions. Additional position heatmaps appear, while selective-trigger results and v1's defended-model accuracy findings are omitted. The shared simulation, circle-count, physical-performance, vehicle-speed, and defense tables retain identical numerical results.

T1.justification: The loss-sign correction in v2 Equation 11 makes minimization mathematically consistent with reducing the original class probability. This is a substantive correction rather than equivalent notation. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: v2 Section 1 adds the explicit claim that fluorescent emission can bypass any filters, extending v1's emphasis on invisibility and selective triggering. The first-use claim for fluorescent ink, three attack goals, and headline 98.31% attack success and 96.72% defense-bypass results remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds a visible-emission explanation for filter resistance and interprets the new distance results as supporting concealed lamp placement and possible drone deployment. It elaborates how previously proposed multi-vehicle collaboration might correct recognition results. The proximity limitation is reframed, while the limitation to component-level rather than autonomous-system evaluation remains.

D1.justification: v2 newly reports 1,500 attack queries and Apple M2 Pro GPU deployment. It omits v1's histogram threshold of 0.05, detector-backbone and CNN-architecture details, and explicit code-access statement, replacing the code-and-video link with a videos-only link. These are documentation changes, not evidence that retained experimental settings changed.

R1.justification: v2 refocuses positioning on attack media and resistance to physical filters. It removes v1's comparative feature table and discussions/citations of shadow, raindrop, and natural-light attacks, while adding a NASA visible-light reference. The principal sticker, projection, infrared, and acoustic attack comparisons remain.

P1.justification: The title and method are renamed, and substantial portions of the introduction, related work, and methodology are rewritten or condensed. The feasibility study moves to Appendix A, digital evaluation to Appendix C, and experimental setup from an appendix into the main text. Ethics material is integrated into the discussion.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column presentation, with extensive figure/table relocation and resizing. v2 removes the prior-work comparison table, localization examples, and selective-trigger figure; adds a viewing-angle schematic and lamp-distance table; expands position heatmaps; and redisplays vehicle-distance plots across the main text and appendix.

improvement.justification: The corrected loss and new lamp-distance evidence improve mathematical consistency and practical validation. However, v2 removes selective-trigger demonstrations, defended-model accuracy results, explicit code-access information, and implementation details, while adding a broad filter-resistance claim without corresponding tests. These gains and losses leave the net quality direction uncertain despite the substantial presentation revision.
